name: Sara Petrov

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We don't sell anything or campaign for a side. Everything here is confidential. What does a normal morning look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The first hour is matching online shop sales to bank deposits while my coffee gets cold. I'm Sara Petrov, forty-three, and I prepare those sellers' accounts and tax returns at Evening Ledger. I have a bachelor's in accounting and years in medical billing, but tax deductions still send me to my supervisor, so I'm a junior here. I use AI every day to draft questions and sort sales, then check the bank record.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What do you enjoy, and what is hard?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like catching a refund before it becomes a client's tax bill. I still need help with unusual deductions and hate sending a question twice. The firm pays me above the usual rate for late video calls with sellers, hours other staff avoid. My partner Mateo runs a catering service, our children are eight and twelve, and we have a mortgage with eleven months saved. There are plenty of other accounting firms near us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take a reliable small saving. I use AI every day to sort marketplace sales and draft questions, but I still compare refunds to the bank before a return goes out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell colleagues to keep what saves time and publish the error list beside it. I'd tell clients that a faster sales report does not replace the person who asks where a refund went.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We'd be comfortable enough in that world. I'm forty-three and a junior at Evening Ledger because tax returns are newer to me than the medical billing I did before. I negotiated a higher rate for late video appointments with sellers, Mateo's catering work adds income, and we have eleven months of expenses saved with plenty of accounting firms nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the daily AI sorting and the supervisor's sign-off on unfamiliar deductions. I'd keep depositing two hundred monthly into the household reserve. In the first year of a plateau, I'd show the team one recurring refund error at our Tuesday meeting and keep the late seller calls on my rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about our mortgage and bills. The work is still demanding, but a small gain does not threaten our way of paying for school and home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What error would you show the team?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A seller refunded a broken lamp, but the platform exported the refund as a fresh sale. The AI report copied it, and my bank check caught it. I printed that page for the next Tuesday meeting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you know a filter works?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd put the sale and bank entries side by side so a junior can see the mismatch. If the supervisor says the new filter fixes it, I'd test the next ten refunds before trusting it. I won't call a green report correct just because it looks tidy.

say: I would show **errors beside savings** from AI sorting before the firm changes any return process.
I would keep **human questions** on client refunds.
think: Our **eleven-month reserve** supports this work even when catering bookings change each season.
Late **seller calls** earn higher pay while I learn tax rules.
do: Keep **daily AI sorting** with supervisor sign-off.
Deposit **two hundred monthly** into the reserve.
Test **ten refunds** before trusting a new filter.
feel: I feel **calm** about our home and income.
S0.quote: I won't call a green report correct just because it looks tidy.
fieldNote: **Late seller appointments** explain high pay without implying strong tax skill.
The **refund mismatch** shows why her daily AI use still needs direct bank checks before a return is signed.

steps.text: Keep daily AI sorting and supervisor review of unfamiliar deductions
Deposit two hundred monthly into household reserve
Test ten refunds before trusting new marketplace filter

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The card names the work on our online-seller desk: checking, writing, booking and answering buyers. If the software does all four, the late video appointments might go away with some junior hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partners to show our error rate and staffing plan together. I'd tell friends a useful tool should earn a fair return for staff and clients, not be a secret reason to cut a rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could keep a role testing the system, but my own late-hour premium might shrink. Mateo's catering contracts are seasonal, so even with eleven months saved we would feel a lasting drop in my higher pay. There are plenty of firms nearby, though they may automate the same desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd pilot the new sale-checker on forty marketplace returns and record false refunds and missed fees. I'd teach two juniors the exception screen if the partners approve paid time. If my hours are cut, I'd apply for a funded payments-control vacancy only if its posted wage covers our mortgage, its start date is signed and school pickup is covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about my own paid hours, though I like testing tools. A pilot can tell me what breaks; it cannot guarantee the partners keep my evening rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would a new rota affect pickup?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mateo covers Wednesday pickup when catering work allows, but a booked event can take him away. I'd ask the school club for a confirmed place before accepting a new evening schedule. I don't want our daughter waiting while we argue about which job was supposed to end first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show the partners?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd take the forty-file error list to the staff meeting with the hours saved next to it. If paid teaching time is refused, I'd still log faults but I would not ask juniors to train after work. A new control role would need a real salary and signed start before I resign.

say: I would publish **errors and staffing** together before the partners change our evening rota.
I would seek **paid teaching time** for juniors.
think: My **late-hour premium** could shrink if software handles routine seller questions.
Seasonal **catering income** makes a lasting pay cut matter.
do: Pilot **forty returns** and log false refunds.
Teach **two juniors** only if paid time is approved; otherwise log faults without asking them to train unpaid.
Apply for **funded controls work** after hour cuts only with written mortgage pay, signed start and confirmed pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my paid rota.
S1.quote: A pilot can tell me what breaks; it cannot guarantee the partners keep my evening rota.
fieldNote: The **forty-file pilot** reflects her comfort testing tools early while tracking faults.
A **controls vacancy** requires funded pay, signed start and confirmed childcare before she moves.

steps.text: Pilot AI sale-checker on forty returns and log missed fees
Teach two juniors if paid time approved; otherwise log faults without unpaid training
Apply for funded controls role after hour cut if written mortgage wage, start, pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI by 2028 could clear our seller returns before my younger child finishes primary school. I know the tools well. Testing the accounting tools does not give me ownership of my tax job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for clear staffing dates and temporary income for displaced workers. I'd also ask the partners to explain who answers when an automated return gives a small shop the wrong tax bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my junior tax post to end in the first year after AGI arrives in 2028. My work is thinking at a screen, so robots around 2031 do not delay that. Mateo's catering service still needs hands-on work for a while, but robots later could reach it, and eleven months saved will not last indefinitely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd pause the extra mortgage repayment and hold its four hundred monthly in cash now. I'd apply for the open adult-college finance post only if it is funded, pays enough, has a signed start and fits our school pickup. In the first year after 2028, if Evening Ledger cuts my job, I'd claim wage support while using our reserve for the regular mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed about losing a high wage, even with nearly a year saved. The other firms may be selling the same cheap automated return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which of your partner’s jobs would you count?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mateo has two catering events signed for next month and three enquiries. I'd count the signed jobs and leave the enquiries out of our mortgage plan. We would tell the children that the summer trip can wait, without using their school savings for an experiment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the college job be safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The college post might also be automated, so I would call it a bridge. I would ask for its posted salary and funded contract before sending my application. If it closes, I keep my current job until a real notice arrives.

say: I would demand **staffing dates** and **temporary income** before junior tax jobs go.
I would ask who owns **wrong automated returns**.
think: My **screen post** could end soon after 2028 despite my daily use of AI.
Eleven months saved may not cover a **market-wide cut**.
do: Hold **four hundred monthly** instead of extra mortgage payments.
Apply for **funded college work** if wage, signed start and pickup fit; if closed, keep current pay and search.
Claim **wage support** after dismissal while reserve pays mortgage.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing a high wage.
S2.quote: Testing the accounting tools does not give me ownership of my tax job.
fieldNote: **Thinking AI** reaches her seller tax desk in 2028, before robots may affect catering work.
The **college fallback** needs funded pay, signed start and pickup while her budget counts only signed catering events.

steps.text: Hold four hundred monthly in cash instead of extra mortgage payments
Apply for funded college role if written mortgage wage, start, pickup fit; if closed stay
Claim wage support after 2028 tax job loss

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years could let me move from preparing returns to checking how a firm tests the software. I wouldn't assume that job is safe after 2031; a strong thinking system may test its own output too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say staff should see error reports and have paid time to learn controls. I'd ask for a written route to an actual vacancy rather than a slogan about future work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A payments-control role might use what I know about bad marketplace feeds. I would still need to learn the wider rules and prove I can spot failures outside my own tax queue. Robots around 2034 do not extend my present screen job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd enrol in the payments-control course if Evening Ledger pays the six-hundred fee and grants paid study hours. I'd test one real merchant case under a controls manager if the client consents and my firm releases me, then ask for written feedback. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if my tax post ends, I'd apply for a funded controls vacancy only after written manager feedback and with advertised mortgage-covering pay, signed start and workable school hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious but interested. Five years is enough to learn the rules if I get actual cases, not just a certificate with my name on it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why ask the firm to fund study?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Six hundred is not beyond our savings, but I would not use family reserve for a course the firm wants on its service list. If it refuses the fee or paid hours, I'd keep my current pay and use free payments-network webinars. I would not call those a substitute for supervised cases.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes the controls case useful?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want a merchant case with the original transaction file and a manager checking my report. A cleaned-up merchant case will not show me where mistakes hide. I'd ask for written feedback before applying to another firm.

say: I would demand **error reports** and paid learning before my return queue disappears.
I would ask for a **written vacancy route**.
think: **Payments controls** might use my seller-file experience, though I still need wider rules.
Full AGI could also test the **software output**.
do: Enrol in **controls study** if fee and hours are paid; otherwise use free webinars while keeping current pay.
Review a **real merchant file** with paid supervision and get written manager feedback.
Apply after **2031 tax job loss** only for funded controls work with mortgage pay, signed start and school hours.
feel: I feel **anxious**, though interested in testing controls.
S3.quote: A cleaned-up merchant case will not show me where mistakes hide.
fieldNote: A **real merchant file** and manager feedback test whether she can work outside tax returns.
The **funded controls role** requires advertised mortgage-covering pay, signed start and school hours after 2031 job loss.

steps.text: Enrol in controls course if firm funds fee and hours; otherwise use free webinars
Review real merchant file if client consents and manager grants paid supervision
Get written manager feedback before applying for outside controls vacancy
Apply for funded controls post after 2031 tax loss if written mortgage pay, start, pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years is enough time to try teaching shop owners how to question an automated sales report. I'd be fifty-three when AGI arrives in 2036, and our children would be nearly grown.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for shorter weeks as returns become quicker and for public training where small firms cannot pay. I'd also want a named person responsible when automated numbers reach a client.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Routine tax returns would still shrink by 2036. A paid teaching slot at the adult college might use my experience, but I would need to see funded classes and a salary that covers our mortgage. Robots around 2039 do not keep my tax desk alive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd teach one paid evening class next spring only if the college has actual enrolment, its fee exceeds my time and childcare costs, and a school-club place is confirmed if Mateo has a catering booking. I'd keep the two-hundred monthly savings transfer and my Evening Ledger wage while testing the class; if no class is funded, I'd try one free library session. In the first year after 2036, if my tax post ends, I'd take a funded teaching vacancy only if its written salary covers our mortgage and the start is signed; otherwise I'd claim support and keep looking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, but not rushed. A decade gives me time to find out whether students actually sign up before I trade a high wage for a classroom.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the class worth your time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the college for a paid slot and a real enrolment list, not applause after a free talk. If no class is funded, I keep my tax wage and try a free library session to learn how I teach. I would not buy teaching equipment on a hoped-for class.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you cover an evening class?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The evening class needs a school-club place for our younger child if Mateo has a catering booking. I'd get that confirmed before agreeing to dates. If the class pays less than the time and childcare cost, I do not take it.

say: I would seek **shorter weeks** and public training while returns still earn the firm money.
I would keep a **named person accountable** for returns.
think: My **tax desk** still shrinks by 2036 despite a decade to build teaching experience.
A **paid teaching class** needs enrolment and mortgage-covering work.
do: Teach a **paid class** only with enrolment, a fee above time and childcare costs, and confirmed school-club cover when Mateo works.
Keep **tax pay** and save two hundred monthly; if class unfunded, try a free library session.
After **2036 tax loss**, take funded teaching work if written mortgage pay and start fit; otherwise claim support and search.
feel: I feel **uneasy** while testing paid demand.
S4.quote: I would not buy teaching equipment on a hoped-for class.
fieldNote: A **paid class** with actual enrolment is her test before changing work.
The **college path** requires funded salary, signed start and confirmed childcare after the tax role ends.

steps.text: Teach paid class only with enrolment, confirmed childcare and fee exceeding time and care costs
Save two hundred monthly and keep tax wage; if class unfunded try free library session
Take funded teaching post after 2036 tax loss if written salary covers mortgage and start confirmed
Claim support and keep searching after 2036 tax loss if no funded teaching post

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my screen work could go before a new paid role is ready. Notice, temporary income, real controls training and a funded vacancy with workable school hours would help. Mateo's signed catering events are real income, but enquiries are not. I cannot put an enquiry in the mortgage account.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask who checks the new checker. If the sales report looks neat but a refund has become a sale, a client can still owe the wrong tax. I want a named person who has time to compare it with the bank.

headlineQuote: I cannot put an enquiry in the mortgage account.
portrait: At **forty-three**, Sara is a junior tax accountant handling online sellers after medical billing work.
Her **accounting bachelor’s** and late calls bring high pay despite tax rules she is still learning.
She uses **AI daily** but checks sales and refunds against bank records.
A **mortgage**, two schoolchildren and eleven months saved give options, with plenty of nearby firms.
She tests **payments controls** and paid teaching only with real cases, enrolment and workable childcare.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her screen job before a funded replacement role is ready.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **notice**, temporary income, real controls training and funded work with workable school hours.
